provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after 'et' before 'te servante'; 1962 sets 'et, te servante,'; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; 1962 writes 'Per Dominum nostrum.'; 1862 layer prints the incipit with no inter-word spacing, 'aUaesumus,omnipotensDeus,' - the ornamental Q is mangled and the spaces are lost; a scan artifact, not a reading; 1862 layer renders the printed stress accents as digits and ampersands throughout (largi6nte, c6rpore, custodi&tur, D6minum); the accents are not evidence here. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 22682-22687, under 'Oratio.' after the Iudica me Introit: 'Quaesumus omnipotens Deus, familiam tuam propitius respice: ut te largiente regatur in corpore: et te servante custodiatur in mente. Per Dominum nostrum.' Long s and the ligatures read as noise there; the 1570 carries the LONGER conclusion, which is the 1962's..

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after 'quaesumus'; 1862 layer reads 'conrilient' for 'concilient' - the c and i of 'conci-' have run together in the scan; the word is corroborated at 1570 line 22876, which reads 'concilient'; 1862 layer reads 'HJEc' for the ornamental Haec. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 22873-22877: 'Haec munera, quaesumus Domine, vincula nostrae pravitatis absolvant: et tuae nobis misericordiae dona concilient. Per Dominum.' The 1570 omits 'et' before 'vincula'; the 1862 and the 1962 both carry it. Cited for the letterforms of 'concilient' and for the prayer being in print before 1931, not for the conjunction.. Recorded limitation: Confidence is medium only because one word, 'concilient', is damaged in the 1862 layer and its letterforms are inferred from the 1570 rather than read. The prayer as a whole is corroborated. The 1862 also prints an 'Altera Secreta' and a pro Papa Secret after it (lines 26713-26727), which are pre-1955 matter and are not taken. No 1862 page image exists for this leaf.
